entries.postTitle: Outgrowing Old Identities

captions.threads:
Success can feel like wearing someone else's skin, and nobody tells you that part.

1/4 I spent years building an identity that looked good from the outside. The credentials stacked up. The audience grew. But somewhere in there, the person I was pretending to be stopped matching the person actually waking up. That gap becomes unbearable.

2/4 Outgrowing an old identity isn't failure. It's your nervous system finally rejecting the mismatch. You start noticing how the old story requires you to shrink, compromise, perform. The energy it takes to maintain that costume becomes unsustainable. That's actually good information.

3/4 Most people fight this feeling. They double down on what worked before, hoping the fit will magically return. But you can't wear last year's skin and expect to breathe properly. The only way through is to let it fall away, even when it terrifies you.

4/4 The person you're becoming doesn't need the old identity's permission. Doesn't need to justify why the previous version doesn't fit anymore. Real work starts when you stop performing for the ghost of who you used to be. That's when you actually get to live.
